newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel thrusts above $7,400, copper edges up.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel thrusts above $7,400, copper edges up.

text.p: Nickel popped higher in LME pre-market activity on Wednesday, extending its bounce of the past two days, but ran into opposition at the highs.
Some of the others edged towards firmer levels, but the general consensus was that higher areas would be difficult to sustain.
Three months nickel peaked at $7,450 per tonne, up $60 from Tuesday's afternoon kerb close, but drifted back to be indicated at $7,400/10.
"There was some Chinese profit-taking at the highs," one trader said.
The market has had a good rebound from lows around $7,100 hit on Monday and it may have done enough on the upside for now, he added.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see it come back a bit, maybe down to $7,300 or $7,250," the trader said.
Copper was firmer in thin early dealings and players were expected to sell into strength.
"People would sell into it up to $2,300, and stop it out if it gets above $2,320," a trader said.
Copper moved up to $2,290, up $9 from Tuesday afternoon. Stocks fell by 1,100 tonnes.
Moderate Far Eastern selling has also been seen over the past few days on any pick-up in prices, traders said.
Aluminium edged up $5 to $1,560 on light short-covering after the market absorbed producer selling on Tuesday.
If the market continues its lacklustre mood, prices are expected to head lower again, with dealer stops said to lurk under $1,550 and fund stops below $1,540.
On any slide, the market would watch closely whether prices held the year's low at $1,534.
Nearby resistance was seen in a band from $1,565/70.
The others were little moved, hovering at largely unchanged levels.
Zinc was up $2 at $1,261 while lead was indicated at $645/47 versus Tuesday's close of $645.
Tin was indicated a touch firmer at $5,765/75 after a previous close of $5,760 and alloy was at $1,452/7 compared to $1,450/55. --Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
